content.title: About
content.content: A graham cracker pie shell is a crisp, lightly sweet base made from whole‑grain flour, sugar, butter and spices. It is a staple in many American desserts, from cheesecakes to fruit tarts.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Graham crackers were created in the early 19th century by Dr. Sylvester Graham as a healthier alternative to regular biscuits.
Traditional recipes use whole‑grain flour, honey and cinnamon, giving the cracker its distinctive aroma.
The shells are often used in no‑bake recipes – the crackers are crushed and mixed with melted butter.
Graham crackers are popular in the US, Canada and Australia, but less common in Europe.
Gluten‑free versions are made from rice or corn flour.

items.title: Source of whole grains
items.content: Whole‑grain flour provides dietary fiber that supports healthy digestion.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Compared with many other cookies, graham crackers contain a moderate amount of fat, making them suitable for calorie‑controlled diets.

items.title: Contains iron and magnesium
items.content: These minerals aid energy metabolism and muscle function.

items.title: Antioxidant spices
items.content: Ingredients such as cinnamon have antioxidant properties.

items.title: Gluten allergy
items.content: Traditional graham crackers contain wheat, so they are not suitable for people with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: The crackers contain added sugar, which should be considered by those monitoring blood glucose.

items.title: Calorie density in large portions
items.content: Consuming large amounts can lead to excess calorie intake.

content.title: How to Use
content.content: Crush the crackers into fine crumbs, combine with melted butter (usually 1:1 by weight), and press into a pan. After chilling, fill with cheesecake, fruit, custard, or any desired filling. The crumbs can also be used as a crunchy topping for ice cream.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the crackers in an airtight container in a cool, dry place. For longer shelf life, keep them in the refrigerator to prevent moisture absorption.
